title: Putnami decision registry v1
$comment: A committed register of settled decisions. The one at the workspace root holds the decisions every project follows; the one in a project directory holds that project's own, and every path it names is relative to that directory. Ids are unique across every registry of a workspace. Each entry carries a stable id, the one-line statement, the date it was settled, who settled it, and either a check `validate` can prove or the `reviewOnly` mark. The format lives in Putnami; the content lives in each repository. Changing a settled value means editing this file in the same change, which makes the re-decision visible in review. An absent file is adoption, never a failure.

protocolVersion.$comment: Readers require the exact JSON integer token 1; 1.0 and 1e0 are invalid.

id.$comment: The stable identity a failure message quotes and a pull request cites. No whitespace, no control character, so the citation is unambiguous.

statement.$comment: The settled value in ONE line. Every failure message quotes it verbatim, so it reads as the rule rather than as a lint code.

settled.$comment: The calendar date the decision was taken, in the one accepted spelling.

adr.$comment: Justification only. The record under the existing doc/adr convention, relative to the registry's directory, explains WHY; it never restates the statement above, so there is no second copy of the rule to drift. It must resolve to a file in the worktree.

reviewOnly.$comment: The mark of a decision no check can prove. It is injected into the generated agent context and never fails a build. Only `true` is meaningful: `false` states neither a check nor a review-only decision and is refused.

jsonValueCheck.$comment: v1 has exactly ONE check kind, and the boundary is deliberate: `json-value` expresses "this declared value is (not) X", which is what the decisions this registry was built for need. Anything it cannot express stays `reviewOnly` until a real decision needs more. Rules nobody has a decision for are not added.

files.$comment: Globs relative to the registry's directory, at least one; they cannot leave it. A whole `**` segment matches zero or more path segments; every other segment never crosses a separator. Zero matching files is SATISFIED: a repository with no such file cannot violate the decision. A matched file that is not valid JSON is a violation naming the parse error, never a skip.

pointer.$comment: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, including the ~0 and ~1 escapes. The empty pointer names the whole document.

rule.$comment: equals is violated when the resolved value differs; notEquals is violated when it matches. Numbers compare by value, so 0, 0.0 and -0 agree, and a resolved object or array never equals a scalar.

whenMissing.$comment: Decides a matched file whose pointer resolves to nothing. Default satisfied: a file that does not declare the member says nothing about the decision. Use violated when the whole point is that the member must be declared.
